meta.system: Isometric Battle Prototype Turn-Based Tactical Combat Spike

objective.technical_goal: Structure a client-side SPA (Vue 3 + PixiJS + Pinia) capable of running a turn-based tactical combat loop on an isometric grid, with deterministic and testable combat logic decoupled from rendering, and a static data layer (SQLite via WASM) validating a database-integration approach for the future full product.
problems_addressed: No combat logic, rendering, or state management exists today, only the default Vite + Vue 3 + TypeScript scaffold

architecture.topology_overview: Client-side layered SPA, no backend, with unidirectional data flow: Pinia is the single source of truth for battle state, composables hold pure combat logic and commit results via actions, and both PixiJS and the Vue/Tailwind HUD read (and write, via composables) the same store without communicating with each other directly.
patterns: Layered architecture with unidirectional data flow (state -> logic -> render/UI)
Separation of state (Pinia), logic (composables), and presentation (Pixi canvas / DOM HUD)

components.name: App Shell (Vue + Vite)
responsibilities: Mounts the configuration screen and the battle screen

components.name: Pixi Renderer (usePixiApp composable)
responsibilities: Owns the Pixi Application and its render loop
Draws tiles, unit sprites, and battle VFX based on store state

components.name: Battle Store (Pinia)
responsibilities: Single source of truth for battle/unit state: stats, HP, status, positions, turn/phase data

components.name: Combat Composables
responsibilities: Pure combat logic: initiative, hit/damage resolution, movement/pathfinding (via the pathfinding package)
Computes results and commits them through Battle Store actions

components.name: Enemy AI Composable
responsibilities: Decides enemy actions (melee approach-and-attack, ranged keep-distance, fallback to Defend/Item)

components.name: HUD (Vue + Tailwind)
responsibilities: DOM overlay: configuration screen, action panels, HP bars
Reads from and writes to the Battle Store via composables

components.name: Animation Layer (GSAP)
responsibilities: Shared timeline/API for canvas animations (movement, attacks) and DOM animations (damage popups, panel transitions)

components.name: Static Data Layer (SQLite via WASM)
responsibilities: Read-only data for Items, Weapons, Upgrades, and Spells
Seeded at build time, queried client-side via SQL

request_flow: HUD captures player input (target/action selection) and calls the corresponding Combat Composable
Combat Composable validates the action (correct turn, target in range/line of sight) against the Battle Store
Composable queries the Static Data Layer for weapon/spell attributes involved in the calculation
Composable runs the pure calculation (hit chance, damage) and calls a Battle Store action to apply the result (HP, status)
Battle Store triggers reactivity; Pixi Renderer and HUD react to the state change
Animation Layer (GSAP) plays the VFX/animation corresponding to the event
data_flow: Origin: player input (HUD) or AI decision (Enemy AI Composable)
Transformation: calculation in Combat Composables combining static data from SQLite with dynamic state from the Battle Store
Destination: Battle Store (mutated state), consumed by Pixi Renderer (drawing) and HUD (display)

relationships: Character references equipped Weapon/Item/Spell (N:1 or N:N)
Character occupies a Tile (1:1 per turn)
BattleState aggregates the list of Characters and the Grid state
data_model.source_of_truth: Dynamic battle data (Character, BattleState, Tile occupancy) in the Pinia Battle Store (in-memory, session-scoped); static data (Weapon, Item, Upgrade, Spell) in SQLite via WASM (read-only, seeded at build time)

strategies: Horizontal scaling fully delegated to Netlify's CDN for serving static assets
Capping the number of simultaneous sprites/effects in the Pixi Renderer to sustain the minimum frame rate
No partitioning/sharding, since there is no distributed data
scalability_availability.caching: Static assets (sprites, audio, JS bundle) via Netlify's standard CDN/browser cache; SQLite data loaded once at startup and kept in memory for the session
scalability_availability.partitioning: Not applicable: SQLite is local and read-only, with no distributed data
scalability_availability.sla_target: Hypothesis: no custom uptime target; follows Netlify's standard free-tier SLA

security.authentication: Not applicable: public application, no login
security.authorization: Not applicable: no distinct roles/permissions, local browser usage only
security.secrets_management: Not applicable: no API keys, credentials, or secrets on the client
security.encryption_in_transit: Not applicable: no sensitive data transmitted
security.encryption_at_rest: Not applicable: battle data lives only in memory during the browser session
security.pii_policy: Not applicable: no personal data is captured or stored

observability.logs: Structured console logging, development environment only, for blocked actions (invalid movement, out-of-range/line-of-sight attacks, out-of-turn actions) and missing VFX/audio assets
metrics: FPS during combat, monitored manually (e.g. via devtools/Pixi stats) as the indicator for the performance NFR
observability.tracing: Not applicable: no distributed calls, the flow is synchronous and local to the browser

risks.risk: Isometric pathfinding complexity (Movement/Jump rules) takes longer than estimated
risks.impact: Delays the prototype, affecting the time/cost measurement goal
mitigation: Implement a simplified version of pathfinding first (without Jump) and evolve it incrementally
Review the movement cost logic in isolation before integrating it with the UI
risks.contingency_plan: If the timeline becomes unsustainable, reduce the Jump rule to a single fixed value (e.g. always 1) and document the simplification as a deviation from the GDD

risks.risk: Runtime performance falls below 30 FPS on weaker machines
risks.impact: Poor experience when demoing the prototype to partners
mitigation: Limit the number of simultaneous sprites/effects
risks.contingency_plan: Reduce VFX quality or grid size if needed

risks.risk: SQLite-via-WASM integration brings unexpected complexity or compatibility issues
risks.impact: Delays the prototype and risks failing to validate this part of the architecture, one of the spike's explicit goals
mitigation: Validate the SQLite + WASM integration in isolation before populating all data
Keep a documented static JSON fallback ready in case WASM proves infeasible within the spike's timeline
risks.contingency_plan: If SQLite via WASM does not work in time, fall back to static JSON temporarily and record the limitation as a learning from the spike

pending_decisions: Exact SQLite/WASM driver to use (e.g. sql.js, wa-sqlite) not yet chosen
Exact SQL schema/serialization format for static data (Items, Weapons, Upgrades, Spells)
next_steps: Detail the data schema (Character, Weapon, Item, Spell, Upgrade)
Specify the public API of the Combat Composables (signatures, inputs/outputs)
Prototype the SQLite/WASM integration in isolation before integrating it with the rest of the system
